subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization, migration - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization, migration - next steps

Hi John / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the embeddings migration and integration items we discussed: 

What we heard
- You currently use Vectorize.ai for embeddings (768-d vectors) and have ~20M records.
- Main goals: reduce similarity-search latency, lower per-query cost, and enable reranking with a contrastive model.
- Primary constraints: batch ingestion window (daily bulk updates), support for streaming/upserts, and preserving existing ranking quality.

Technical items & recommendations
- Vector dimensions: Redwood supports multiple open models and dims — we recommend moving to a 1536-d embedding (Open embedding families) only if your reranker or downstream models expect that dimension. If you migrate to 1536 you can improve recall but will increase storage/cost ~2x. Alternative: stay on 768 and use our optimized ANN index with tuned recall/latency.
- Batching: For bulk migration, use our batched upsert API with suggested batch size 2k–5k vectors per request depending on your instance size. We also offer a managed streaming ingestion path for near-real-time updates.
- Normalization: We strongly recommend L2-normalizing vectors server-side at ingest for cosine sims. We can do this transparently in Redwood or you can normalize client-side; we'll include the normalization flag in the SDK/sample scripts.
- Migration from Vectorize.ai: two options — (1) cold bulk export + batched upsert into Redwood; (2) live-sync using our change-data-capture connector to do phased cutover. We advised a canary subset (5–10%) first to validate ranking.
- Rerankers: Our platform supports reranker scoring pipelines (embedding similarity -> reranker model). If you want re-ranking with a contrastive model, we'll align dims or add a projection layer.
- Auth & SDK: We provide SDKs (Python/Node) that handle auth (API key / service account) and automatic retries. For Private deployments we support service-account JWTs and KMS-backed keys.

Attachments: I attached a short migration_playbook.pdf and a csv with rough benchmark baselines.

Next steps
1) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Ethan (solutions engineer) to cover batch sizing, index config, and a migration runbook — propose Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13.
2) Share a small sample export (10k records) so we can run a baseline embed + ANN run and return latency/recall numbers.
3) We'll provision a trial project and provide instructions to load test ingestion (redwood_trial_instructions.txt attached).

If that plan looks good, I'll get a calendar invite out and Evan/I will prepare a short test plan.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: vector dims, batching, normalization, migration - next steps

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick tech notes I want captured before the deep-dive: 

- Batch sizing: the 2k–5k guideline assumes medium-sized GPU nodes (g4dn/rtx class). If ACME's Dedicated pools are smaller (e.g. 8GB GPU memory), we'll recommend 500–1k per batch. We'll validate in the deep-dive.
- Ingest pipeline: recommend a small pre-processing step to dedupe records and compute a stable id mapping (acme_id -> redwood_id). This simplifies upserts and rollback.
- Dimensional mismatch: if current vectors are 768 and you want to move to 1536, migrating by recomputing embeddings is safest. We can support on-the-fly projection but it can cause quality drift; we'll quantify in the trial.
- Normalization & ANN: we should enable server-side L2 normalization and use HNSW index with efConstruction tuned for recall 0.95. I'll bring suggested hyperparameters to the call.
- Auth: for the trial we'll provision an API key scoped to the trial project with a short TTL and IP restrictions. For production, recommend service-account-based flows.

I'll prepare a one-pager with the suggested ingestion code snippet (Python) and the HNSW defaults.

Ethan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.ai

John —

Great questions. Short answers and what we'll cover on Thu 8/13 11am PT: 

1) Latency/recall samples: we'll run 10k sample baselines for both 768 and 1536 with HNSW defaults and share a one-page table (latency p50/p95, recall@10, storage). I attached embedding_benchmarks.csv with tentative numbers; we'll replace with ACME-specific results after your sample.
2) Partial failures: the SDK supports idempotent upserts and a per-batch retry with exponential backoff (base 500ms, max 30s). For partial failures we return failed ids so you can retry selectively; we'll include a reconciliation script in the playbook.
3) Normalization: normalizing server-side still preserves vector geometry for cosine — you can continue on-device scoring as long as you apply the same normalization. We'll include sample code for client-side and server-side normalization.
4) RTO/RPO for live-sync: typical phased cutover (sync -> mirror -> cut) yields RPO = seconds (if streaming enabled) and RTO depends on index warm-up (we advise a canary 5–10% to validate). We'll go over rollback steps and the canary plan.

Pilot pricing: we do offer pilot credits and a migration assistance package for mid-contract migrations — I'll loop in our Sales Ops contact after the call to discuss details and paperwork.

Confirmed: Thu 8/13, 11:00am PT works for our team. I'll send the invite and include a short agenda: 1) ingestion + batching configs, 2) index & reranker strategy, 3) migration runbook & pilot terms.

Thanks — looking forward.
